comments.body:
Pushed for review as Gerrit change 1383 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1383).

Fix widens rebar search to match by identifier: reducer/search.py::_haystack now folds in ticket_id, alias, and a new optional jira_key field (all lowercased, single substring path). The reducer stays pure — the caller _engine_support/reads.py::search_state builds a ticket_id->jira_key map once from the binding store reverse index (new _ids.py::binding_jira_key_map, sharing the JSON loader _load_binding_reverse with _resolve_via_binding_store) and annotates each state before calling search_states. Matching is case-folded on both sides so 'search REB-1654' and 'search reb-1654' both surface the bound ticket, mirroring 'show'. Tests: tests/unit/test_search_identifiers.py (pure search_states units incl. case-insensitivity + no-leak) and two integration tests in tests/interfaces/queries/test_ws5a_search.py (ticket_id/alias and bound Jira-key at the CLI seam); all RED-first on origin/main. make lint + make typecheck green; touched files well under the 800 LOC cap. Not closing pending Verified +1 (green CI) and LLM-Review +1.

compiled_state.description:
# `rebar search` does not match tickets by their identifiers (ticket id, alias, or bound Jira key)

## Context / Problem

`rebar search` is full-text over a narrow haystack. `reducer/search.py::_haystack`
builds the searchable text from ONLY `title`, `description`, `tags`, and each comment
`body`. It excludes every IDENTIFIER a user is most likely to paste into search:

- the canonical `ticket_id` (e.g. `0303-692c-55dc-4a18`),
- the human `alias` (e.g. `doctorial-semiironic-wrasse`),
- the bound **Jira key** (e.g. `REB-1654`).

Concrete footgun (observed 2026-08-04): `rebar show REB-1654` correctly resolves to
`0303-692c-55dc-4a18` (via `_ids.py::resolve_ticket_id` -> `_resolve_via_binding_store`),
but `rebar search "REB-1654"` returns `[]`. A user who reaches for `search` with an
identifier gets nothing and may wrongly conclude the ticket does not exist. The same holds
for a full ticket id or an alias substring.

## Root-cause mechanism (cited)

- `_haystack` never adds `ticket_id`/`alias`, and the reduced state carries NO Jira key at
  all: the Jira binding lives in the binding store, read only by
  `_ids.py::_resolve_via_binding_store` (the `.bridge_state` reverse map ticket_id -> jira_key).
- `reducer/search.py::search_states` is deliberately pure (operates on state dicts); the
  enrichment seam is the caller `_engine_support/reads.py::search_state` (line ~456), which
  already injects a `parent_resolver`: the analogous place to fold identifiers in.
- Matching is case-folded: `_haystack` returns `.lower()`. Any identifier added to the
  haystack must be lowercased, AND a query typed as `REB-1654` (uppercase) must still match:
  verify `_query.parse_query` lowercases free-text terms; if it does not, lower the compared
  term for the id path so `show`/`search` accept the same input casing.

## Approach

1. Extend `_haystack` (or add an identifier segment it concatenates) to include
   `state.get("ticket_id")`, `state.get("alias")`, and a new optional
   `state.get("jira_key")` field, all lowercased, matching existing behavior.
2. Enrich states with their bound Jira key in the caller `search_state`
   (`_engine_support/reads.py`): build the ticket_id -> jira_key map ONCE from the binding
   store's reverse map (the same source `_resolve_via_binding_store` reads) and annotate each
   reduced state before calling `search_states`. Keep `search_states` pure: do not make it
   read the filesystem/binding store.
3. Guarantee case-insensitivity for identifier queries so `search REB-1654` and
   `search reb-1654` both surface the bound ticket.

Do NOT change the predicate/filter grammar (`_query.parse_query`, `_filters`): this is a
haystack widening only. Do NOT special-case identifier matches as "exact"; folding them into
the substring haystack is sufficient and keeps one matching path.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/reducer/search.py` - `_haystack` gains the identifier segment.
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py` - `search_state` enriches states with `jira_key`.
- A tiny accessor to read the binding reverse map without duplicating `_ids` internals
  (reuse the existing one if present; cite it).
- Tests below.

## Testing (RED first - each fails on current main for the right reason)

- `search_states` unit: a state carrying `ticket_id`/`alias`/`jira_key` is returned when the
  query is that ticket_id, that alias, or that Jira key (each its own case), and is NOT
  returned for an unrelated identifier. Drive the match, not a mock.
- case-insensitivity: querying the UPPERCASE Jira key (`REB-1654`) matches a state whose
  bound key is `REB-1654` (proves the fold on both sides).
- integration at the `search_state`/CLI seam: a ticket bound to a Jira key is discoverable by
  `rebar search <JIRA-KEY>` (mirrors `rebar show <JIRA-KEY>` resolving it): the exact
  reported footgun, RED-verified by reverting the enrichment.
- pinned-unchanged: existing free-text search over title/description/comments/tags returns
  the same results (no regression to the historical whitespace-AND substring path); the
  predicate grammar tests stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar search` matches a ticket by its canonical `ticket_id`, its `alias`, and its
      bound Jira key - checked by new unit tests on `search_states` (RED-first) and an
      integration test at the `search_state` seam mirroring `show <JIRA-KEY>`.
- [ ] identifier matching is case-insensitive (`REB-1654` and `reb-1654` both match) -
      checked by a dedicated test.
- [ ] `search_states` stays pure (no filesystem/binding-store access inside it); the Jira-key
      enrichment happens in the caller - checked by the enrichment living in
      `_engine_support/reads.py` and the unit tests passing on hand-built states.
- [ ] existing full-text search and the predicate/filter grammar are unchanged - checked by
      the pre-existing search tests staying green with zero edits.
compiled_state.title: rebar search does not match by ticket id, alias, or bound Jira key
